title: Sunny and the Kookaburra
author: Jamie Wigg
the_end_text:
The End.
Sweet dreams, little one. Goodnight.
back_cover_blurb: As the golden dusk settles over the sleepy bush, little Sunny the quokka meets a gentle kookaburra saying goodnight to the day. Together they watch the sky turn to deep plum, count the first soft stars, and let their eyes grow heavy. A calm, cosy bedtime tale for winding down and drifting off to sleep. Perfect for little ones ages 1-5.

pages.scene: Sunny the little quokka stands in a soft clearing of the Australian bush at dusk, tall gum trees around her glowing in warm honey-gold light. The sky is a gentle wash of gold sinking into deep plum-navy. A few early fireflies drift near her round cheeks, and she gazes up with sleepy, kind eyes.
pages.text: The sun was slipping low, and the whole bush turned warm and golden. Little Sunny the quokka came out to say goodnight to the day.

pages.scene: Sunny pads softly through cool moonlit grass between tall gum trees, honey-gold light fading to plum-navy overhead, fireflies twinkling gently around her paws. Her small ears are perked, listening, and her face is calm and curious in the hush.
pages.text: The bush was growing quiet and cosy. Sunny's tummy felt calm, and her steps were slow and soft.

pages.scene: Sunny pauses beneath a great gum tree, one paw lifted, tilting her head to listen. Warm dusk light filters through the leaves in gold and deep plum, the first faint star glimmering above. A soft, drowsy sound seems to float on the evening air.
pages.text: Then she heard it — a soft, laughing sound, gentle as a yawn. “Koo-koo-ka-ha,” it hummed, slow and sleepy.

pages.scene: Sunny looks up toward a high gum branch where a warm shape is nestled against the plum-navy sky. Golden light glows on the tree trunk, fireflies rising slowly, first stars appearing. Sunny's eyes are wide with quiet wonder, not fear.
pages.text: The sound was not loud at all. It was soft and kind, like someone getting cosy for the night.

pages.scene: Close view of a chunky kookaburra perched on a mossy gum branch, its large head and big beak silhouetted against a honey-gold and plum-navy dusk sky. Its cream and brown feathers glow softly in the warm light. Below, little Sunny the quokka peeks up from the grass, fireflies drifting between them.
pages.text: High on a branch sat a kookaburra, round and cosy, with a big head and a friendly beak. Its feathers were cream and soft brown.

pages.scene: The kookaburra tilts its large head gently down toward Sunny, who stands in the grass below looking up. Warm golden dusk fades to deep plum-navy, gum leaves rustle softly, fireflies glow between them. Both faces are calm and sleepy.
pages.text: “Good evening, little one,” said the kookaburra, in a low, drowsy voice. “Hello,” whispered Sunny, with a soft smile.

pages.scene: Sunny sits down comfortably in the moonlit grass at the foot of the gum tree, gazing up at the kookaburra on its branch. The sky above them deepens from honey-gold to plum-navy, more stars appearing, fireflies twinkling all around in the warm hush.
pages.text: Sunny sat down in the cool grass to rest. “Are you getting ready for bed?” she asked.

pages.scene: The kookaburra settles a little on its branch, feathers gently fluffed, big beak lowered in a calm, sleepy pose. The dusk sky glows deep plum-navy behind it with soft gold at the horizon, first stars out, fireflies drifting. Sunny watches contentedly below.
pages.text: “I am,” said the kookaburra softly. “Every evening, I say goodnight to the sun before I sleep.”

pages.scene: The kookaburra opens its beak just a little and gives one small, gentle chuckle toward the last glow of golden light at the horizon. The sky is mostly deep plum-navy now with a warm band of gold. Sunny listens, ears soft, fireflies floating around the gum branch.
pages.text: It gave one last soft chuckle, ever so quiet. “Koo-ka-ha,” it hummed. “That is my sleepy goodnight to the day.”

pages.scene: The kookaburra tucks and smooths its cream and brown feathers with its big beak, settling deeper into the mossy gum branch. Warm dusk light is almost gone, replaced by soft plum-navy and gentle stars. Fireflies drift lazily. Sunny watches with heavy, happy eyes.
pages.text: Then the kookaburra tidied its soft feathers, one by one, until they were all cosy and warm.

pages.scene: Sunny gazes upward as the sky slowly changes color, honey-gold melting into deep plum and navy above the tall gum trees. The very first bright stars twinkle out. Fireflies glow gently around the quokka and the settling kookaburra. Everything is calm and still.
pages.text: Together they watched the sky turn from gold to soft plum, and then to deep, quiet blue.

pages.scene: A wide, peaceful view of the bush at nightfall: tall gum trees in silhouette against a deep plum-navy sky sprinkled with the first stars. The kookaburra is cosy on its branch, Sunny small and content in the grass below, fireflies twinkling like tiny lanterns.
pages.text: One by one, the first stars came out, soft and shining. “The bush is going to sleep,” Sunny whispered.

pages.scene: The bush grows hushed and still around Sunny and the kookaburra. Gum leaves are quiet, the plum-navy sky deepens, more stars appear. Fireflies drift slowly. Sunny lets out a tiny, gentle yawn, her eyes half-closed and content.
pages.text: The whole bush grew hushed and still. Sunny gave a tiny yawn, and her eyes felt soft and heavy.

pages.scene: The kookaburra rests its big head down against its cosy cream and brown feathers, eyes gently closing, tucked on the mossy gum branch under a star-filled plum-navy sky. Sunny looks up sleepily from the grass, fireflies glowing warmly around them both.
pages.text: The kookaburra nestled down, its big head sinking into its warm feathers. “Sleep is coming for us both,” it murmured.

pages.scene: Sunny and the drowsy kookaburra share a calm, sleepy look beneath the tall gum trees. The sky is deep plum-navy, full of gentle stars, and a soft round moon begins to rise. Fireflies twinkle slowly. Both look peaceful and ready for rest.
pages.text: Sunny smiled up at her new friend. Her heart felt warm and calm, all the way through.

pages.scene: Sunny stands and gives a gentle little wave with her paw toward the kookaburra tucked cosy on its branch. The moon glows soft and round in the plum-navy sky, stars scattered above the gum trees, fireflies drifting. A tender, quiet goodnight moment.
pages.text: “Goodnight, kookaburra,” Sunny whispered softly. “Goodnight, little quokka,” it hummed, already half asleep.

pages.scene: Sunny pads home through silvery moonlit grass, tall gum trees standing calm and dark against a deep plum-navy sky full of stars. The round moon lights her gentle path, fireflies floating beside her. She walks slowly, sleepy and content.
pages.text: Sunny padded home through the cool, moonlit grass, soft and quiet under the gentle stars.

pages.scene: Sunny arrives at her cosy little burrow nestled among the roots of a great gum tree. Warm, soft light glows from inside. The plum-navy night sky twinkles above, the moon round and calm, fireflies drifting near her home. Sunny yawns sleepily at her doorway.
pages.text: At last she reached her cosy little home among the gum tree roots. Everything was warm and safe.

pages.scene: Sunny curls up snugly in her soft, warm bed inside the burrow, tucked in cosy. A little round window shows the deep plum-navy sky, stars, and the gentle moon outside. Fireflies glow faintly beyond the glass. Her eyes are closed, her face peaceful and smiling.
pages.text: Sunny curled up in her soft, warm bed and closed her sleepy eyes. The night was calm and still.

pages.scene: Sunny sleeps peacefully in her cosy burrow, a small dreamy image of the gentle kookaburra floating above her like a soft cloud. The plum-navy night is full of stars and the round moon, fireflies twinkling. Everything is warm, safe, and quiet.
pages.text: And as she drifted off to sleep, Sunny dreamed of the gentle kookaburra, softly laughing the day goodnight.
